<DESCRIPTION>KAMADA REPORTS STRONG SECOND QUARTER AND FIRST HALF 2024 FINANCIAL RESULTS WITH YEAR-OVER-YEAR 6-MONTH TOP-LINE GROWTH OF 18% AND A 68% INCREASE IN PROFITABILITY
<TEXT>
<HTML>
<HEAD>
     <TITLE></TITLE>
</HEAD>
<BODY STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif">

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: right"><B>Exhibit 99.1</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><B>Kamada Reports Strong Second Quarter and First
Half 2024 Financial Results with Year-Over-Year 6-Month Top-Line Growth of 18% and a 68% Increase in Profitability</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; width: 100%"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in; text-align: left"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#9679;</FONT></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><I>Revenues for Second Quarter of 2024 were $42.5 Million, up 13% Year-over-Year; First Half 2024 Total Revenues
were $80.2 Million, up 18% Year-over-Year</I></FONT></TD>
</TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; width: 100%"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in; text-align: left"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#9679;</FONT></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><I>Second Quarter 2024 Adjusted EBITDA of $9.1 Million, Representing 51% Increase Year-over-Year; First Half 2024
Adjusted EBITDA of $16.6 Million, up 68% Year-over-Year</I></FONT></TD>
</TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; width: 100%"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in; text-align: left"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#9679;</FONT></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><I>Robust First Half 2024 Performance and Expectation for Similar Cadence of Financial Results for Second Half of
the Year Supports Reiteration of Full-Year Revenue Guidance of $158 Million-$162 Million and Adjusted EBITDA of $28 Million-$32 Million</I></FONT></TD>
</TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; width: 100%"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in; text-align: left"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#9679;</FONT></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><I>Conference Call and Live Webcast Today at 8:30 AM ET</I></FONT></TD>
</TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>REHOVOT, Israel, and Hoboken, NJ &ndash; August
14, 2024</B> -- Kamada Ltd. (NASDAQ: KMDA; TASE: KMDA.TA), a global biopharmaceutical company with a portfolio of marketed products indicated
for rare and serious conditions and a leader in the specialty plasma-derived field, today announced financial results for the three and
six months ended June 30, 2024.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&ldquo;<FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif">Our <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">strong financial performance is
indicative of the successful execution of our growth strategy as we continue to effectively leverage our multiple diverse commercial catalysts,
including our six FDA-approved products,&rdquo; said Amir London, Kamada&rsquo;s Chief Executive Officer. &ldquo;With total revenues for
the first half of 2024 of $80.2 million, which represents year-over-year growth of 18%, adjusted EBITDA of $16.6 million, up 68% year-over-year
and representing a 21% margin of revenues, <FONT STYLE="background-color: white">we achieved the top- and bottom-line profitable growth
anticipated in our business.</FONT> In addition, during the first six months of the year, we generated $15.0 million of cash provided
by operating activities, which demonstrates our ability to convert our reported adjusted EBITDA to operational cash flow.</FONT>&rdquo; </FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&ldquo;Based on our <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">continued strong performance
and expectation for a cadence of financial results in the second half of 2024 consistent with those achieved in the first six months of
the year, we are reiterating our full-year 2024 revenue guidance of $158 million to $162 million, and our adjusted EBITDA guidance of
$28 million to $32 million. Importantly, we continue to pursue compelling new business development opportunities, leveraging our financial
strength. These opportunities are expected to support continued growth at double-digit rates beyond 2024,&rdquo; added Mr. London</FONT>.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&ldquo;Patient enrollment continues in our ongoing pivotal Phase 3 InnovAATe clinical trial for the inhaled Alpha-1
Antitrypsin <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">therapy. Last quarter, we filed an IND amendment
with the FDA consisting of a revised Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) and study protocol, which, if approved, may allow for the acceleration
of the program. We continue to expect further FDA feedback before the end of this year,&rdquo; concluded Mr. London</FONT>.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>Financial Highlights for the Three Months Ended
June 30, 2024</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; width: 100%"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<TD STYLE="width: 0in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in; text-align: left"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif">&#9679;</FONT></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif">Total
revenues were $42.5 million in the second quarter of 2024, a 13% increase from the prior year comparable quarter. <FONT STYLE="background-color: white">The
increase in revenues was primarily attributable to increased sales of KEDRAB due to increased market share in the U.S</FONT>., as well
as increased <FONT STYLE="background-color: white">sales of CYTOGAM due to increased demand in the U.S. market.</FONT></FONT></TD>
</TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; width: 100%"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<TD STYLE="width: 0in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in; text-align: left"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif">&#9679;</FONT></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif">Gross
profit and gross margins were $19.0 million and 45%, respectively, in the second quarter of 2024, compared to $14.4 million and 39%,
respectively, reported in the prior year comparable quarter.</FONT></TD>
</TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"></P>

costs associated with <FONT STYLE="background-color: white">the marketing activities in the U.S., </FONT>as well as increased R&amp;D

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">As of June 30, 2024, the Company had cash, cash
equivalents, and short-term investments of $56.5 million, as compared to $55.6 million on December 31, 2023.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>Fiscal Year 2024 Guidance</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Kamada continues to expect to generate fiscal
year 2024 total revenues in the range of $158 million to $162 million, and adjusted EBITDA in the range of $28 million to $32 million,
representing double digit top- and bottom-line growth year-over-year.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>Non-IFRS financial measures</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">We present EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA because
we use these non-IFRS financial measures to assess our operational performance, for financial and operational decision-making, and as
a means to evaluate period-to-period comparisons on a consistent basis. Management believes these non-IFRS financial measures are useful
to investors because: (1) they allow for greater transparency with respect to key metrics used by management in its financial and operational
decision-making and provide investors with a meaningful perspective on the current underlying performance of the Company&rsquo;s core
ongoing operations; and (2) they exclude the impact of certain items that are not directly attributable to our core operating performance
and that may obscure trends in the core operating performance of the business. Non-IFRS financial measures have limitations as an analytical
tool and should not be considered in isolation from, or as a substitute for, our IFRS results. We expect to continue reporting non-IFRS
financial measures, adjusting for the items described below, and we expect to continue to incur expenses similar to certain of the non-cash,
non-IFRS adjustments described below. Accordingly, unless otherwise stated, the exclusion of these and other similar items in the presentation
of non-IFRS financial measures should not be construed as an inference that these items are unusual, infrequent or non-recurring. EBITDA
and adjusted EBITDA are not recognized terms under IFRS and do not purport to be an alternative to IFRS terms as an indicator of operating
performance or any other IFRS measure. Moreover, because not all companies use identical measures and calculations, the presentation of
EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA may not be comparable to other similarly titled measures of other companies. EBITDA is defined as net income
(loss), plus income tax expense, plus or minus financial income or expenses, net, plus or minus income or expense in respect of securities
measured at fair value, net, plus or minus income or expenses in respect of currency exchange differences and derivatives instruments,
net, plus depreciation and amortization expense, whereas adjusted EBITDA is the EBITDA plus non-cash share-based compensation expenses
and certain other costs.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">For the projected 2024 adjusted EBITDA information
presented herein, the Company is unable to provide a reconciliation of this forward measure to the most comparable IFRS financial measure
because the information for these measures is dependent on future events, many of which are outside of the Company&rsquo;s control. Additionally,
estimating such forward-looking measures and providing a meaningful reconciliation consistent with the Company&rsquo;s accounting policies
for future periods is meaningfully difficult and requires a level of precision that is unavailable for these future periods and cannot
be accomplished without unreasonable effort.&nbsp; Forward-looking non-IFRS measures are estimated in a manner consistent with the relevant
definitions and assumptions noted in the Company&rsquo;s adjusted EBITDA for historical periods.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>About Kamada </B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Kamada Ltd. (the &ldquo;Company&rdquo;) is a
global biopharmaceutical company with a portfolio of marketed products indicated for rare and serious conditions and a leader in the
specialty plasma-derived field, focused on diseases of limited treatment alternatives. The Company is also advancing an innovative development
pipeline targeting areas of significant unmet medical need. The Company&rsquo;s strategy is focused on driving profitable growth from
its significant commercial catalysts as well as its manufacturing and development expertise in the plasma-derived and biopharmaceutical
fields. The Company&rsquo;s commercial products portfolio includes six FDA approved plasma-derived biopharmaceutical products: CYTOGAM<SUP><SUP>&reg;</SUP></SUP>,
KEDRAB<SUP><SUP>&reg;</SUP></SUP>, WINRHO SDF<SUP>&reg;</SUP>, VARIZIG<SUP>&reg;</SUP>, HEPAGAM B<SUP>&reg;</SUP> and GLASSIA<SUP>&reg;</SUP>, as well as KAMRAB<SUP>&reg;</SUP>, KAMRHO (D)<SUP>&reg;</SUP> and two
types of equine-based anti-snake venom (ASV) products. The Company distributes its commercial products portfolio directly, and through
strategic partners or third-party distributors in more than 30 countries, including the U.S., Canada, Israel, Russia, Argentina, Brazil,
India, Australia and other countries in Latin America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia. The Company leverages its expertise and presence
in the Israeli market to distribute, for use in Israel, more than 25 pharmaceutical products that are supplied by international manufacturers.
During recent years the Company added eleven biosimilar products to its Israeli distribution portfolio, which, subject to the European
Medicines Agency (EMA) and the Israeli Ministry of Health approvals, are expected to be launched in Israel through 2028. The Company
owns an FDA licensed plasma collection center in Beaumont, Texas, which currently specializes in the collection of hyper-immune plasma
used in the manufacture of KAMRHO (D), KARAB and KEDRAB. In addition to the Company&rsquo;s commercial operation, it invests in research
and development of new product candidates. The Company&rsquo;s leading investigational product is an inhaled AAT for the treatment of
AAT deficiency, for which it is continuing to progress the InnovAATe clinical trial, a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled,
pivotal Phase 3 trial. FIMI Opportunity Funds, the leading private equity firm in Israel, is the Company&rsquo;s controlling shareholder,
beneficially owning approximately 38% of the outstanding ordinary shares.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

</div><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" escape="true" name="ifrs-full:DisclosureOfGeneralInformationAboutFinancialStatementsExplanatory" id="ixv-5411"><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>Note 1:- General</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline">General description of the Company
and its activity</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">Kamada Ltd. (the &#8220;Company&#8221;)
is a commercial stage global biopharmaceutical company with a portfolio of marketed products indicated for rare and serious conditions
and a leader in the specialty plasma-derived field focused on diseases of limited treatment alternatives. The Company is also advancing
an innovative development pipeline targeting areas of significant unmet medical need. The Company&#8217;s strategy is focused on driving
profitable growth from its significant commercial catalysts as well as its manufacturing and development expertise in the plasma-derived
and biopharmaceutical fields. The Company&#8217;s commercial products portfolio includes six FDA approved plasma-derived biopharmaceutical
products KEDRAB&#174;, CYTOGAM&#174;, VARIZIG&#174;, WINRHO SDF&#174;, HEPAGAM B&#174; and GLASSIA&#174;, as well as KAMRAB&#174;, KAMRHO (D)&#174;
and two types of equine-based anti-snake venom (ASV) products. The Company distributes its commercial products portfolio directly, and
through strategic partners or third-party distributors in more than 30 countries, including the U.S., Canada, Israel, Russia, Argentina,
Brazil, India, Australia and other countries in Latin America, Europe, the Middle East and Asia. The Company leverages its expertise and
presence in the Israeli market to distribute, for use in Israel, more than 25 pharmaceutical products that are supplied by international
manufacturers and in addition have eleven biosimilar products in its Israeli distribution portfolio, which, subject to European Medicines
Agency (EMA) and Israeli Ministry of Health (&#8220;IL MOH&#8221;) approvals, are expected to be launched in Israel through 2028. The
Company owns an FDA licensed plasma collection center in Beaumont, Texas, which currently specializes in the collection of hyper-immune
plasma used in the manufacture of KAMRHO (D), KAMRAB and KEDRAB. In addition to the Company&#8217;s commercial operation, it invests in
research and development of new product candidates. The Company&#8217;s leading investigational product is an inhaled AAT for the treatment
of AAT deficiency, for which it is continuing to progress the InnovAATe clinical trial, a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled,
pivotal Phase 3 trial.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">In November 2021, the Company acquired
CYTOGAM, WINRHO SDF, VARIZIG and HEPGAM B from Saol Therapeutics Ltd. (&#8220;Saol&#8221;). The acquisition of this portfolio furthered
the Company&#8217;s core objective to become a fully integrated specialty plasma company with strong commercial capabilities in the U.S.
market, as well as to expand to new markets, mainly in the Middle East/North Africa region, and to broaden the Company&#8217;s portfolio
offering in existing markets. The Company&#8217;s wholly owned U.S. subsidiary, Kamada Inc., is responsible for the commercialization
of the four products in the U.S. market, including direct sales to wholesalers and local distributers. Refer to Note 5 in our annual Financial
report for further details on this acquisition.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">The Company markets GLASSIA in the U.S.
through a strategic partnership with Takeda Pharmaceuticals Company Limited (&#8220;Takeda&#8221;). Historically, the Company generated
revenues on sales of GLASSIA, manufactured by the Company, to Takeda for further distribution in the United States. In accordance with
the agreement with Takeda, the Company ceased the production and sale of GLASSIA to Takeda during 2021, and during the first quarter of
2022, Takeda began to pay the Company royalties on sales of GLASSIA manufactured by Takeda, at a rate of <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c1" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="ifrs-full:BorrowingsInterestRate" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-7907">12</ix:nonFraction>% on net sales through August
2025 and at a rate of <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c88" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="ifrs-full:BorrowingsInterestRate" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-7908">6</ix:nonFraction>% thereafter until 2040, with a minimum of $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c0" decimals="-6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="kmda:AnnualAmount" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7909">5</ix:nonFraction> million annually for each of the years from 2022 to 2040. Refer to
Note 18 in our annual Financial report for further details on the engagement with Takeda.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">The Company&#8217;s ordinary shares are
listed for trading on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange and the NASDAQ Global Select Market.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">FIMI Opportunity Funds (&#8220;FIMI&#8221;),
the leading private equity firm in Israel beneficially owns approximately <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c0" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="kmda:PercentageOfOutstandingOrdinaryShares" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-7910">38</ix:nonFraction>% of the Company&#8217;s outstanding ordinary shares and is
a controlling shareholder of the Company; within the meaning of the Israeli Companies Law, 1999. Refer to Note 20 for further details
and Item 7 within the Company annual reports on Form 20-F.</p></ix:nonNumeric><div>

</div><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" escape="true" name="ifrs-full:DisclosureOfChangesInAccountingPoliciesExplanatory" id="ixv-5453"><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>Note 2:- Significant Accounting Policies</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 56.7pt; text-indent: -56.7pt"><b>&#160;</b></p>

<ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" continuedAt="_DisclosureOfBasisOfPreparationOfFinancialStatementsExplanatory-c0_cont_1" escape="true" name="ifrs-full:DisclosureOfBasisOfPreparationOfFinancialStatementsExplanatory" id="ixv-5458"><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%"> <tr style="vertical-align: top"> <td style="width: 0.5in">&#160;</td> <td style="width: 0.25in"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">a.</span></td> <td style="text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Basis of preparation of the interim consolidated financial statements:</span></td></tr> </table></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>&#160;&#160;</b></p>

<ix:continuation id="_DisclosureOfBasisOfPreparationOfFinancialStatementsExplanatory-c0_cont_1"><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify">The interim consolidated financial
statements have been prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles for the preparation of financial statements
for interim periods, as prescribed in IAS 34, &#8220;Interim Financial Reporting&#8221;.</p></ix:continuation>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 28.35pt; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" continuedAt="kmda_ImplementationOfNewAccountingStandardsPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_1" escape="true" name="kmda:ImplementationOfNewAccountingStandardsPolicyTextBlock" id="ixv-5471"><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%"> <tr style="vertical-align: top"> <td style="width: 0.5in">&#160;</td> <td style="width: 0.25in"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">b.</span></td> <td style="text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Implementation of new accounting standards:</span></td></tr> </table></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<ix:continuation continuedAt="kmda_ImplementationOfNewAccountingStandardsPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_2" id="kmda_ImplementationOfNewAccountingStandardsPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_1"><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 76px">&#160;</td>
    <td style="text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>Amendment to IAS 1, <i>Presentation of Financial Statements: Classification of Liabilities as Current or Non-Current</i> and subsequent amendment: <i>Non-Current Liabilities with Covenants</i></b></span></td></tr>
  </table></ix:continuation>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<ix:continuation continuedAt="kmda_ImplementationOfNewAccountingStandardsPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_3" id="kmda_ImplementationOfNewAccountingStandardsPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_2"><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify">The Amendment, together with the subsequent
amendment to IAS 1 (see hereunder) replaces certain requirements for classifying liabilities as current or non-current. According to the
Amendment, a liability will be classified as non-current when the entity has the right to defer settlement for at least 12 months after
the reporting period, and it &#8220;has substance&#8221; and is in existence at the end of the reporting period. According to the subsequent
amendment, as published in October 2022, covenants with which the entity must comply after the reporting date do not affect classification
of the liability as current or non-current. Additionally, the subsequent amendment adds disclosure requirements for liabilities subject
to covenants within 12 months after the reporting date, such as disclosure regarding the nature of the covenants, the date they need to
be complied with and facts and circumstances that indicate the entity may have difficulty complying with the covenants. Furthermore, the
Amendment clarifies that the conversion option of a liability will affect its classification as current or non-current, other than when
the conversion option is recognized as equity.</p></ix:continuation>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<ix:continuation continuedAt="kmda_ImplementationOfNewAccountingStandardsPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_4" id="kmda_ImplementationOfNewAccountingStandardsPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_3"><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify">The Amendment and subsequent amendment
are effective for reporting periods beginning on or after January 1, 2024 with earlier application being permitted. The Amendment and
subsequent amendment are applicable retrospectively, including an amendment to comparative data.</p></ix:continuation>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.6in; text-align: justify"><span style="text-decoration:line-through;text-decoration: none">&#160;</span></p>

<ix:continuation continuedAt="kmda_ImplementationOfNewAccountingStandardsPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_5" id="kmda_ImplementationOfNewAccountingStandardsPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_4"><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify">As of June 30, 2024, the Company does
not have impact on its financial statement.</p></ix:continuation>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">&#160;&#160;</p>

<ix:continuation continuedAt="kmda_ImplementationOfNewAccountingStandardsPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_6" id="kmda_ImplementationOfNewAccountingStandardsPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_5"><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 0.75in">&#160;</td>
    <td style="text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>IFRS 18, <i>Presentation and Disclosure in Financial Statements</i></b></span></td></tr>
  </table></ix:continuation>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<ix:continuation continuedAt="kmda_ImplementationOfNewAccountingStandardsPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_7" id="kmda_ImplementationOfNewAccountingStandardsPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_6"><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify">This standard replaces IAS 1, Presentation
of Financial Statements. The purpose of the standard is to provide improved structure and content to the financial statements, particularly
the income statement.</p></ix:continuation>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<ix:continuation continuedAt="kmda_ImplementationOfNewAccountingStandardsPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_8" id="kmda_ImplementationOfNewAccountingStandardsPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_7"><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify">The standard includes new disclosure and
presentation requirements that were taken from IAS 1, Presentation of Financial Statements, with small changes.</p></ix:continuation>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<ix:continuation continuedAt="kmda_ImplementationOfNewAccountingStandardsPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_9" id="kmda_ImplementationOfNewAccountingStandardsPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_8"><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify">As part of the new disclosure requirements,
companies will be required to present two subtotals in the income statement: operating profit and profit before financing and taxes. Furthermore,
for most companies, the results in the income statements will be classified into three categories: operating profit, profit from investments
and profit from financing.</p></ix:continuation>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<ix:continuation continuedAt="kmda_ImplementationOfNewAccountingStandardsPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_10" id="kmda_ImplementationOfNewAccountingStandardsPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_9"><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify">In addition to the changes in the structure
of the income statements, the standard also includes a requirement to provide separate disclosure in the financial statements regarding
the use of management-defined performance measures (non-GAAP measures).</p></ix:continuation>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<ix:continuation continuedAt="kmda_ImplementationOfNewAccountingStandardsPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_11" id="kmda_ImplementationOfNewAccountingStandardsPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_10"><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify">Furthermore, the standard adds specific
guidance for aggregation and disaggregation of items in the financial statements and in the notes. The standard will encourage companies
to avoid classifying items as &#8216;other&#8217; (for example, other expenses), and using this classification will lead to additional
disclosure requirements.</p></ix:continuation>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<ix:continuation continuedAt="kmda_ImplementationOfNewAccountingStandardsPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_12" id="kmda_ImplementationOfNewAccountingStandardsPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_11"><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify">The standard is effective from annual
reporting periods beginning on or after January 1, 2027 with earlier application being permitted.</p></ix:continuation>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<ix:continuation id="kmda_ImplementationOfNewAccountingStandardsPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_12"><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify">The Company is examining the effects of
the standard on its financial statements with no plans for early adoption.</p></ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p><div>

<th class="tl" colspan="1" rowspan="2"><div style="width: 200px;"><strong>General<br></strong></div></th>
<th class="th" colspan="1">6 Months Ended</th>
</tr>
<tr><th class="th"><div>Jun. 30, 2024</div></th></tr>
<tr class="re">
<td class="pl" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="Show.showAR( this, 'defref_ifrs-full_NotesAndOtherExplanatoryInformationAbstract', window );"><strong>General [Abstract]</strong></a></td>
<td class="text">&#160;<span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="ro">
<td class="pl" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="Show.showAR( this, 'defref_ifrs-full_DisclosureOfGeneralInformationAboutFinancialStatementsExplanatory', window );">General</a></td>
<td class="text"><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>Note 1:- General</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline">General description of the Company
and its activity</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">Kamada Ltd. (the &#8220;Company&#8221;)
is a commercial stage global biopharmaceutical company with a portfolio of marketed products indicated for rare and serious conditions
and a leader in the specialty plasma-derived field focused on diseases of limited treatment alternatives. The Company is also advancing
an innovative development pipeline targeting areas of significant unmet medical need. The Company&#8217;s strategy is focused on driving
profitable growth from its significant commercial catalysts as well as its manufacturing and development expertise in the plasma-derived
and biopharmaceutical fields. The Company&#8217;s commercial products portfolio includes six FDA approved plasma-derived biopharmaceutical
products KEDRAB&#174;, CYTOGAM&#174;, VARIZIG&#174;, WINRHO SDF&#174;, HEPAGAM B&#174; and GLASSIA&#174;, as well as KAMRAB&#174;, KAMRHO (D)&#174;
and two types of equine-based anti-snake venom (ASV) products. The Company distributes its commercial products portfolio directly, and
through strategic partners or third-party distributors in more than 30 countries, including the U.S., Canada, Israel, Russia, Argentina,
Brazil, India, Australia and other countries in Latin America, Europe, the Middle East and Asia. The Company leverages its expertise and
presence in the Israeli market to distribute, for use in Israel, more than 25 pharmaceutical products that are supplied by international
manufacturers and in addition have eleven biosimilar products in its Israeli distribution portfolio, which, subject to European Medicines
Agency (EMA) and Israeli Ministry of Health (&#8220;IL MOH&#8221;) approvals, are expected to be launched in Israel through 2028. The
Company owns an FDA licensed plasma collection center in Beaumont, Texas, which currently specializes in the collection of hyper-immune
plasma used in the manufacture of KAMRHO (D), KAMRAB and KEDRAB. In addition to the Company&#8217;s commercial operation, it invests in
research and development of new product candidates. The Company&#8217;s leading investigational product is an inhaled AAT for the treatment
of AAT deficiency, for which it is continuing to progress the InnovAATe clinical trial, a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled,
pivotal Phase 3 trial.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">In November 2021, the Company acquired
CYTOGAM, WINRHO SDF, VARIZIG and HEPGAM B from Saol Therapeutics Ltd. (&#8220;Saol&#8221;). The acquisition of this portfolio furthered
the Company&#8217;s core objective to become a fully integrated specialty plasma company with strong commercial capabilities in the U.S.
market, as well as to expand to new markets, mainly in the Middle East/North Africa region, and to broaden the Company&#8217;s portfolio
offering in existing markets. The Company&#8217;s wholly owned U.S. subsidiary, Kamada Inc., is responsible for the commercialization
of the four products in the U.S. market, including direct sales to wholesalers and local distributers. Refer to Note 5 in our annual Financial
report for further details on this acquisition.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">The Company markets GLASSIA in the U.S.
through a strategic partnership with Takeda Pharmaceuticals Company Limited (&#8220;Takeda&#8221;). Historically, the Company generated
revenues on sales of GLASSIA, manufactured by the Company, to Takeda for further distribution in the United States. In accordance with
the agreement with Takeda, the Company ceased the production and sale of GLASSIA to Takeda during 2021, and during the first quarter of
2022, Takeda began to pay the Company royalties on sales of GLASSIA manufactured by Takeda, at a rate of 12% on net sales through August
2025 and at a rate of 6% thereafter until 2040, with a minimum of $5 million annually for each of the years from 2022 to 2040. Refer to
Note 18 in our annual Financial report for further details on the engagement with Takeda.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">The Company&#8217;s ordinary shares are
listed for trading on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange and the NASDAQ Global Select Market.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">FIMI Opportunity Funds (&#8220;FIMI&#8221;),
the leading private equity firm in Israel beneficially owns approximately 38% of the Company&#8217;s outstanding ordinary shares and is
a controlling shareholder of the Company; within the meaning of the Israeli Companies Law, 1999. Refer to Note 20 for further details
and Item 7 within the Company annual reports on Form 20-F.</p><span></span>
</td>
</tr>

<span style="display: none;">v3.24.2.u1</span><table class="report" border="0" cellspacing="2" id="idm139651378130160">
<tr>
<th class="tl" colspan="1" rowspan="2"><div style="width: 200px;"><strong>Significant Accounting Policies<br></strong></div></th>
<th class="th" colspan="1">6 Months Ended</th>
</tr>
<tr><th class="th"><div>Jun. 30, 2024</div></th></tr>
<tr class="re">
<td class="pl" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="Show.showAR( this, 'defref_kmda_SignificantAccountingPolicieAbstract', window );"><strong>Significant Accounting Policies [Abstract]</strong></a></td>
<td class="text">&#160;<span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="ro">
<td class="pl" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="Show.showAR( this, 'defref_ifrs-full_DisclosureOfChangesInAccountingPoliciesExplanatory', window );">Significant Accounting Policies</a></td>
<td class="text"><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>Note 2:- Significant Accounting Policies</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 56.7pt; text-indent: -56.7pt"><b>&#160;</b></p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%"> <tr style="vertical-align: top"> <td style="width: 0.5in">&#160;</td> <td style="width: 0.25in"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">a.</span></td> <td style="text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Basis of preparation of the interim consolidated financial statements:</span></td></tr> </table>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>&#160;&#160;</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify">The interim consolidated financial
statements have been prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles for the preparation of financial statements
for interim periods, as prescribed in IAS 34, &#8220;Interim Financial Reporting&#8221;.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 28.35pt; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%"> <tr style="vertical-align: top"> <td style="width: 0.5in">&#160;</td> <td style="width: 0.25in"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">b.</span></td> <td style="text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Implementation of new accounting standards:</span></td></tr> </table>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 76px">&#160;</td>
    <td style="text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>Amendment to IAS 1, <i>Presentation of Financial Statements: Classification of Liabilities as Current or Non-Current</i> and subsequent amendment: <i>Non-Current Liabilities with Covenants</i></b></span></td></tr>
  </table>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify">The Amendment, together with the subsequent
amendment to IAS 1 (see hereunder) replaces certain requirements for classifying liabilities as current or non-current. According to the
Amendment, a liability will be classified as non-current when the entity has the right to defer settlement for at least 12 months after
the reporting period, and it &#8220;has substance&#8221; and is in existence at the end of the reporting period. According to the subsequent
amendment, as published in October 2022, covenants with which the entity must comply after the reporting date do not affect classification
of the liability as current or non-current. Additionally, the subsequent amendment adds disclosure requirements for liabilities subject
to covenants within 12 months after the reporting date, such as disclosure regarding the nature of the covenants, the date they need to
be complied with and facts and circumstances that indicate the entity may have difficulty complying with the covenants. Furthermore, the
Amendment clarifies that the conversion option of a liability will affect its classification as current or non-current, other than when
the conversion option is recognized as equity.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify">The Amendment and subsequent amendment
are effective for reporting periods beginning on or after January 1, 2024 with earlier application being permitted. The Amendment and
subsequent amendment are applicable retrospectively, including an amendment to comparative data.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.6in; text-align: justify"><span style="text-decoration:line-through;text-decoration: none">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify">As of June 30, 2024, the Company does
not have impact on its financial statement.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">&#160;&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 0.75in">&#160;</td>
    <td style="text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>IFRS 18, <i>Presentation and Disclosure in Financial Statements</i></b></span></td></tr>
  </table>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify">This standard replaces IAS 1, Presentation
of Financial Statements. The purpose of the standard is to provide improved structure and content to the financial statements, particularly
the income statement.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify">The standard includes new disclosure and
presentation requirements that were taken from IAS 1, Presentation of Financial Statements, with small changes.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify">As part of the new disclosure requirements,
companies will be required to present two subtotals in the income statement: operating profit and profit before financing and taxes. Furthermore,
for most companies, the results in the income statements will be classified into three categories: operating profit, profit from investments
and profit from financing.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify">In addition to the changes in the structure
of the income statements, the standard also includes a requirement to provide separate disclosure in the financial statements regarding
the use of management-defined performance measures (non-GAAP measures).</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify">Furthermore, the standard adds specific
guidance for aggregation and disaggregation of items in the financial statements and in the notes. The standard will encourage companies
to avoid classifying items as &#8216;other&#8217; (for example, other expenses), and using this classification will lead to additional
disclosure requirements.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify">The standard is effective from annual
reporting periods beginning on or after January 1, 2027 with earlier application being permitted.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify">The Company is examining the effects of
the standard on its financial statements with no plans for early adoption.</p><span></span>
</td>
</tr>
</table>

<td class="text"><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 56.7pt; text-indent: -56.7pt"><b>Note 4:- Operating Segments</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 56.7pt; text-indent: -56.7pt"><b>&#160;</b></p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 0.5in">&#160;</td>
    <td style="width: 0.25in"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">a.</span></td>

<td class="text">&#160;<span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="ro">
<td class="pl" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="Show.showAR( this, 'defref_ifrs-full_DisclosureOfBasisOfPreparationOfFinancialStatementsExplanatory', window );">Basis of preparation of the interim consolidated financial statements</a></td>
<td class="text"><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%"> <tr style="vertical-align: top"> <td style="width: 0.5in">&#160;</td> <td style="width: 0.25in"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">a.</span></td> <td style="text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Basis of preparation of the interim consolidated financial statements:</span></td></tr> </table><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify">The interim consolidated financial
statements have been prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles for the preparation of financial statements
for interim periods, as prescribed in IAS 34, &#8220;Interim Financial Reporting&#8221;.</p><span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="re">
<td class="pl custom" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="Show.showAR( this, 'defref_kmda_ImplementationOfNewAccountingStandardsPolicyTextBlock', window );">Implementation of new accounting standards</a></td>
<td class="text"><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%"> <tr style="vertical-align: top"> <td style="width: 0.5in">&#160;</td> <td style="width: 0.25in"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">b.</span></td> <td style="text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Implementation of new accounting standards:</span></td></tr> </table><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 76px">&#160;</td>
    <td style="text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>Amendment to IAS 1, <i>Presentation of Financial Statements: Classification of Liabilities as Current or Non-Current</i> and subsequent amendment: <i>Non-Current Liabilities with Covenants</i></b></span></td></tr>
  </table><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify">The Amendment, together with the subsequent
amendment to IAS 1 (see hereunder) replaces certain requirements for classifying liabilities as current or non-current. According to the
Amendment, a liability will be classified as non-current when the entity has the right to defer settlement for at least 12 months after
the reporting period, and it &#8220;has substance&#8221; and is in existence at the end of the reporting period. According to the subsequent
amendment, as published in October 2022, covenants with which the entity must comply after the reporting date do not affect classification
of the liability as current or non-current. Additionally, the subsequent amendment adds disclosure requirements for liabilities subject
to covenants within 12 months after the reporting date, such as disclosure regarding the nature of the covenants, the date they need to
be complied with and facts and circumstances that indicate the entity may have difficulty complying with the covenants. Furthermore, the
Amendment clarifies that the conversion option of a liability will affect its classification as current or non-current, other than when
the conversion option is recognized as equity.</p><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify">The Amendment and subsequent amendment
are effective for reporting periods beginning on or after January 1, 2024 with earlier application being permitted. The Amendment and
subsequent amendment are applicable retrospectively, including an amendment to comparative data.</p><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify">As of June 30, 2024, the Company does
not have impact on its financial statement.</p><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 0.75in">&#160;</td>
    <td style="text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>IFRS 18, <i>Presentation and Disclosure in Financial Statements</i></b></span></td></tr>
  </table><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify">This standard replaces IAS 1, Presentation
of Financial Statements. The purpose of the standard is to provide improved structure and content to the financial statements, particularly
the income statement.</p><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify">The standard includes new disclosure and
presentation requirements that were taken from IAS 1, Presentation of Financial Statements, with small changes.</p><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify">As part of the new disclosure requirements,
companies will be required to present two subtotals in the income statement: operating profit and profit before financing and taxes. Furthermore,
for most companies, the results in the income statements will be classified into three categories: operating profit, profit from investments
and profit from financing.</p><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify">In addition to the changes in the structure
of the income statements, the standard also includes a requirement to provide separate disclosure in the financial statements regarding
the use of management-defined performance measures (non-GAAP measures).</p><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify">Furthermore, the standard adds specific
guidance for aggregation and disaggregation of items in the financial statements and in the notes. The standard will encourage companies
to avoid classifying items as &#8216;other&#8217; (for example, other expenses), and using this classification will lead to additional
disclosure requirements.</p><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify">The standard is effective from annual
reporting periods beginning on or after January 1, 2027 with earlier application being permitted.</p><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify">The Company is examining the effects of
the standard on its financial statements with no plans for early adoption.</p><span></span>
</td>
</tr>
</table>

<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>Number of operating segments. An operating segment is a component of an enterprise: (a) that engages in business activities from which it may earn revenues and incur expenses (including revenues and expenses relating to transactions with other components of the same enterprise), (b) whose operating results are regularly reviewed by the enterprise's chief operating decision maker to make decisions about resources to be allocated to the segment and assess its performance, and (c) for which discrete financial information is available. An operating segment may engage in business activities for which it has yet to earn revenues, for example, start-up operations may be operating segments before earning revenues.</p></div>
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="Show.toggleNext( this );">+ References</a><div style="display: none;"><p>No definition available.</p></div>

    <ifrs-full:DisclosureOfGeneralInformationAboutFinancialStatementsExplanatory contextRef="c0" id="ixv-5411">&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Note 1:- General&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"&gt;&lt;span style="text-decoration:underline"&gt;General description of the Company
and its activity&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"&gt;Kamada Ltd. (the &#x201c;Company&#x201d;)
is a commercial stage global biopharmaceutical company with a portfolio of marketed products indicated for rare and serious conditions
and a leader in the specialty plasma-derived field focused on diseases of limited treatment alternatives. The Company is also advancing
an innovative development pipeline targeting areas of significant unmet medical need. The Company&#x2019;s strategy is focused on driving
profitable growth from its significant commercial catalysts as well as its manufacturing and development expertise in the plasma-derived
and biopharmaceutical fields. The Company&#x2019;s commercial products portfolio includes six FDA approved plasma-derived biopharmaceutical
products KEDRAB&#xae;, CYTOGAM&#xae;, VARIZIG&#xae;, WINRHO SDF&#xae;, HEPAGAM B&#xae; and GLASSIA&#xae;, as well as KAMRAB&#xae;, KAMRHO (D)&#xae;
and two types of equine-based anti-snake venom (ASV) products. The Company distributes its commercial products portfolio directly, and
through strategic partners or third-party distributors in more than 30 countries, including the U.S., Canada, Israel, Russia, Argentina,
Brazil, India, Australia and other countries in Latin America, Europe, the Middle East and Asia. The Company leverages its expertise and
presence in the Israeli market to distribute, for use in Israel, more than 25 pharmaceutical products that are supplied by international
manufacturers and in addition have eleven biosimilar products in its Israeli distribution portfolio, which, subject to European Medicines
Agency (EMA) and Israeli Ministry of Health (&#x201c;IL MOH&#x201d;) approvals, are expected to be launched in Israel through 2028. The
Company owns an FDA licensed plasma collection center in Beaumont, Texas, which currently specializes in the collection of hyper-immune
plasma used in the manufacture of KAMRHO (D), KAMRAB and KEDRAB. In addition to the Company&#x2019;s commercial operation, it invests in
research and development of new product candidates. The Company&#x2019;s leading investigational product is an inhaled AAT for the treatment
of AAT deficiency, for which it is continuing to progress the InnovAATe clinical trial, a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled,
pivotal Phase 3 trial.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"&gt;In November 2021, the Company acquired
CYTOGAM, WINRHO SDF, VARIZIG and HEPGAM B from Saol Therapeutics Ltd. (&#x201c;Saol&#x201d;). The acquisition of this portfolio furthered
the Company&#x2019;s core objective to become a fully integrated specialty plasma company with strong commercial capabilities in the U.S.
market, as well as to expand to new markets, mainly in the Middle East/North Africa region, and to broaden the Company&#x2019;s portfolio
offering in existing markets. The Company&#x2019;s wholly owned U.S. subsidiary, Kamada Inc., is responsible for the commercialization
of the four products in the U.S. market, including direct sales to wholesalers and local distributers. Refer to Note 5 in our annual Financial
report for further details on this acquisition.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"&gt;The Company markets GLASSIA in the U.S.
through a strategic partnership with Takeda Pharmaceuticals Company Limited (&#x201c;Takeda&#x201d;). Historically, the Company generated
revenues on sales of GLASSIA, manufactured by the Company, to Takeda for further distribution in the United States. In accordance with
the agreement with Takeda, the Company ceased the production and sale of GLASSIA to Takeda during 2021, and during the first quarter of
2022, Takeda began to pay the Company royalties on sales of GLASSIA manufactured by Takeda, at a rate of 12% on net sales through August
2025 and at a rate of 6% thereafter until 2040, with a minimum of $5 million annually for each of the years from 2022 to 2040. Refer to
Note 18 in our annual Financial report for further details on the engagement with Takeda.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"&gt;The Company&#x2019;s ordinary shares are
listed for trading on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange and the NASDAQ Global Select Market.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"&gt;FIMI Opportunity Funds (&#x201c;FIMI&#x201d;),
the leading private equity firm in Israel beneficially owns approximately 38% of the Company&#x2019;s outstanding ordinary shares and is
a controlling shareholder of the Company; within the meaning of the Israeli Companies Law, 1999. Refer to Note 20 for further details
and Item 7 within the Company annual reports on Form 20-F.&lt;/p&gt;</ifrs-full:DisclosureOfGeneralInformationAboutFinancialStatementsExplanatory>

    <ifrs-full:DisclosureOfChangesInAccountingPoliciesExplanatory contextRef="c0" id="ixv-5453">&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Note 2:- Significant Accounting Policies&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 56.7pt; text-indent: -56.7pt"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&#160;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%"&gt; &lt;tr style="vertical-align: top"&gt; &lt;td style="width: 0.5in"&gt;&#160;&lt;/td&gt; &lt;td style="width: 0.25in"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"&gt;a.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt; &lt;td style="text-align: justify"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"&gt;Basis of preparation of the interim consolidated financial statements:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt; &lt;/table&gt;
&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&#160;&#160;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify"&gt;The interim consolidated financial
statements have been prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles for the preparation of financial statements
for interim periods, as prescribed in IAS 34, &#x201c;Interim Financial Reporting&#x201d;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 28.35pt; text-align: justify"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%"&gt; &lt;tr style="vertical-align: top"&gt; &lt;td style="width: 0.5in"&gt;&#160;&lt;/td&gt; &lt;td style="width: 0.25in"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"&gt;b.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt; &lt;td style="text-align: justify"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"&gt;Implementation of new accounting standards:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt; &lt;/table&gt;
&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%"&gt;
  &lt;tr style="vertical-align: top"&gt;
    &lt;td style="width: 76px"&gt;&#160;&lt;/td&gt;
    &lt;td style="text-align: justify"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Amendment to IAS 1, &lt;i&gt;Presentation of Financial Statements: Classification of Liabilities as Current or Non-Current&lt;/i&gt; and subsequent amendment: &lt;i&gt;Non-Current Liabilities with Covenants&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;
  &lt;/table&gt;
&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify"&gt;The Amendment, together with the subsequent
amendment to IAS 1 (see hereunder) replaces certain requirements for classifying liabilities as current or non-current. According to the
Amendment, a liability will be classified as non-current when the entity has the right to defer settlement for at least 12 months after
the reporting period, and it &#x201c;has substance&#x201d; and is in existence at the end of the reporting period. According to the subsequent
amendment, as published in October 2022, covenants with which the entity must comply after the reporting date do not affect classification
of the liability as current or non-current. Additionally, the subsequent amendment adds disclosure requirements for liabilities subject
to covenants within 12 months after the reporting date, such as disclosure regarding the nature of the covenants, the date they need to
be complied with and facts and circumstances that indicate the entity may have difficulty complying with the covenants. Furthermore, the
Amendment clarifies that the conversion option of a liability will affect its classification as current or non-current, other than when
the conversion option is recognized as equity.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify"&gt;The Amendment and subsequent amendment
are effective for reporting periods beginning on or after January 1, 2024 with earlier application being permitted. The Amendment and
subsequent amendment are applicable retrospectively, including an amendment to comparative data.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.6in; text-align: justify"&gt;&lt;span style="text-decoration:line-through;text-decoration: none"&gt;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify"&gt;As of June 30, 2024, the Company does
not have impact on its financial statement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"&gt;&#160;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%"&gt;
  &lt;tr style="vertical-align: top"&gt;
    &lt;td style="width: 0.75in"&gt;&#160;&lt;/td&gt;
    &lt;td style="text-align: justify"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"&gt;&lt;b&gt;IFRS 18, &lt;i&gt;Presentation and Disclosure in Financial Statements&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;
  &lt;/table&gt;
&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify"&gt;This standard replaces IAS 1, Presentation
of Financial Statements. The purpose of the standard is to provide improved structure and content to the financial statements, particularly
the income statement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify"&gt;The standard includes new disclosure and
presentation requirements that were taken from IAS 1, Presentation of Financial Statements, with small changes.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify"&gt;As part of the new disclosure requirements,
companies will be required to present two subtotals in the income statement: operating profit and profit before financing and taxes. Furthermore,
for most companies, the results in the income statements will be classified into three categories: operating profit, profit from investments
and profit from financing.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify"&gt;In addition to the changes in the structure
of the income statements, the standard also includes a requirement to provide separate disclosure in the financial statements regarding
the use of management-defined performance measures (non-GAAP measures).&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify"&gt;Furthermore, the standard adds specific
guidance for aggregation and disaggregation of items in the financial statements and in the notes. The standard will encourage companies
to avoid classifying items as &#x2018;other&#x2019; (for example, other expenses), and using this classification will lead to additional
disclosure requirements.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify"&gt;The standard is effective from annual
reporting periods beginning on or after January 1, 2027 with earlier application being permitted.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify"&gt;The Company is examining the effects of
the standard on its financial statements with no plans for early adoption.&lt;/p&gt;</ifrs-full:DisclosureOfChangesInAccountingPoliciesExplanatory>
    <ifrs-full:DisclosureOfBasisOfPreparationOfFinancialStatementsExplanatory contextRef="c0" id="ixv-5458">&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%"&gt; &lt;tr style="vertical-align: top"&gt; &lt;td style="width: 0.5in"&gt;&#160;&lt;/td&gt; &lt;td style="width: 0.25in"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"&gt;a.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt; &lt;td style="text-align: justify"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"&gt;Basis of preparation of the interim consolidated financial statements:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt; &lt;/table&gt;&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify"&gt;The interim consolidated financial
statements have been prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles for the preparation of financial statements
for interim periods, as prescribed in IAS 34, &#x201c;Interim Financial Reporting&#x201d;.&lt;/p&gt;</ifrs-full:DisclosureOfBasisOfPreparationOfFinancialStatementsExplanatory>

  &lt;tr style="vertical-align: top"&gt;
    &lt;td style="width: 76px"&gt;&#160;&lt;/td&gt;
    &lt;td style="text-align: justify"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Amendment to IAS 1, &lt;i&gt;Presentation of Financial Statements: Classification of Liabilities as Current or Non-Current&lt;/i&gt; and subsequent amendment: &lt;i&gt;Non-Current Liabilities with Covenants&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;
  &lt;/table&gt;&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify"&gt;The Amendment, together with the subsequent
amendment to IAS 1 (see hereunder) replaces certain requirements for classifying liabilities as current or non-current. According to the
Amendment, a liability will be classified as non-current when the entity has the right to defer settlement for at least 12 months after
the reporting period, and it &#x201c;has substance&#x201d; and is in existence at the end of the reporting period. According to the subsequent
amendment, as published in October 2022, covenants with which the entity must comply after the reporting date do not affect classification
of the liability as current or non-current. Additionally, the subsequent amendment adds disclosure requirements for liabilities subject
to covenants within 12 months after the reporting date, such as disclosure regarding the nature of the covenants, the date they need to
be complied with and facts and circumstances that indicate the entity may have difficulty complying with the covenants. Furthermore, the
Amendment clarifies that the conversion option of a liability will affect its classification as current or non-current, other than when
the conversion option is recognized as equity.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify"&gt;The Amendment and subsequent amendment
are effective for reporting periods beginning on or after January 1, 2024 with earlier application being permitted. The Amendment and
subsequent amendment are applicable retrospectively, including an amendment to comparative data.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify"&gt;As of June 30, 2024, the Company does
not have impact on its financial statement.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%"&gt;
